_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Contemporary Six
suggestions.reason: Alex Reuben's original room on Princess Street, by the Town Hall's side door — forty-odd artists on rotation, an Own Art scheme that lets you pay monthly, and the space that later gave Hale its own quieter twin.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, confidentials.com and Tripadvisor (2025 reviews still current): Contemporary Six, 37 Princess Street, Manchester M2 4FN, founded by Alex Reuben in 2010, still trading and representing around 40 artists. Coordinates are the real M2 4FN postcode centroid, geographically closer to Chinatown's own district centroid (53.4792/-2.2400) than Deansgate's, so assigned there. This is the original Manchester gallery whose second room (Contemporary Six Hale, in the space Clark Art left behind) is already a real venue in docs/data/venues.json — same sibling-gallery precedent already established for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields/Cibo. No other locations found beyond these two. High confidence — well-documented, long-running, multiple independent sources agree it's currently open.

suggestions.name: K2 Karaoke
suggestions.reason: Thirty private booths across two George Street floors, right in the middle of the streets that are Chinatown before Chinatown is anything else — the one real answer here to a night that wants its own soundtrack.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via K2's own site (k2karaoke.com), Tripadvisor (2026 reviews, still listed as trading) and Yelp: 52-56 George Street, Manchester M1 4HF — confirmed single site, no other K2 Karaoke locations found anywhere else in the UK. George Street is one of the three streets (with Nicholas Street and Faulkner Street) that define Chinatown's real core per Wikipedia's own Chinatown, Manchester entry, so the district assignment is a genuine geographic fit, not a stretch. Fills a real gap: Chinatown had only one Drink-category venue (Bar Shrimp) before this. Introduces a new type, KARAOKE BAR, left Drink category-only for now — no existing onboarding tile fits precisely, same treatment as ALE HOUSE/WINE MERCHANT elsewhere in venues.json. Moderate-high confidence — real, currently trading, clearly non-chain, but a genuinely different register (loud, groups, booths) from most of this file's curated picks, flagged for the reviewer's own judgment on fit.

suggestions.name: Pip
suggestions.reason: Mary-Ellen McTague's return to the city she left Aumbry in, cooking low-waste, seasonal British plates on the ground floor of the Treehouse — a Michelin Guide listing within its first year.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Michelin Guide's own 2025 listing, manchestersfinest.com, designmynight.com and treehousehotels.com: Pip, Treehouse Hotel, Blackfriars Street, Manchester M3 2EQ, led by chef Mary-Ellen McTague (previously Aumbry, The Creameries). The restaurant concept itself is single-site — the only chain footprint is the Treehouse Hotel brand it sits inside (a small boutique group with a handful of international properties), which this file's own precedent (Refuge inside the Kimpton, Podium inside Hotel Gotham/Cloud23) already treats as not disqualifying, since the actual dining concept and its ownership/kitchen are independent of the hotel brand. High confidence — extensively covered, recent, clearly still trading.

suggestions.name: Portfolio
suggestions.reason: Julian Pizer and Cameron Foster's own cellar made public on Bridge Street — 250-odd Champagnes from more than seventy growers, a wall of a hundred bottles to read while you decide, and a menu of single-bite dishes built to match whichever one you land on.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via themanc.com, eatnorth.co.uk, classbarmag.com and thatsup.co.uk: Portfolio, 67-69 Bridge Street, Manchester M3 3BQ — confirmed by postcode lookup to sit within Spinningfields itself ('M3 3BQ is a non-residential postcode in Spinningfields, Manchester'). Billed as the UK's first dedicated Champagne boutique/bar, opened by Julian Pizer (co-owner of Another Hand, already a real venue in docs/data/venues.json's Deansgate entries) and Cameron Foster (Deux Six) — single site, no other locations found. Fills a real gap: Spinningfields had only 2 Drink-category venues out of 8 before this. Uses the existing CHAMPAGNE BAR type (first introduced for Bacchus, Prestbury), which already maps to the real 'Champagne bars' onboarding tile. High confidence — heavily covered at opening by multiple independent local food/drink press outlets, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: HARCOURT
suggestions.reason: Brian and Priscilla Hung's Hong Kong-inspired free house on Stamford New Road — fourteen taps of proper cask and craft, and small plates built from Hong Kong's own street-food repertoire rather than a brewery's set menu.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA's own listing (a real 14-tap modern beer bar entry), confidentials.com's review, Hardens and thegoodfoodguide.co.uk: Harcourt, 80 Stamford New Road, Altrincham WA14 1BS, launched 2024 by Brian and Priscilla Hung — single independent site, free-of-tie per CAMRA (not a brewery tied house, the pattern already excluded elsewhere in this file for Robinsons/Hydes pubs). No other Harcourt locations found. Uses the existing GASTROPUB type (Wilmslow Tavern, Charlie Brown's Hale precedent), which CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE treats as Eat despite the pub format — consistent with that existing precedent even though this venue reads more beer-forward than food-forward. High confidence — CAMRA-verified, multiple 2024-2025 reviews, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Butchers Bar
suggestions.reason: Turtons' old shop on Ashley Road, empty three years, reborn as Ben Shepherd's own stage and skylight — cocktails poured at the counter where the meat used to hang, and live sets most nights rather than a jukebox.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via altrincham.todaynews.co.uk's opening coverage and the venue's own site/Instagram (thebutchersbarhale.com, @thebutchersbarhale): Butchers Bar opened in the former Turtons of Hale butchers, 181 Ashley Road, Hale WA15 9SD, with a soft launch 30 April 2026 and official opening 1 May 2026 — founded by Ben Shepherd (also founder of the Tipple Tea drinks brand, not a venue chain). Single site, real and recently opened, no closure signals (too new for any). Fills a real gap: Hale needed more Drink-category coverage. Introduces a new type, LIVE MUSIC BAR, left Drink category-only — no existing onboarding tile fits a general (non-jazz) live-music-and-cocktails bar precisely; the existing 'Live music' Do tile only maps to pure arts venues (Band on the Wall, Hope Mill Theatre), not a bar. Moderate confidence — real and well-documented at opening, but only ~4 months of trading history to judge staying power against.

suggestions.name: Neki
suggestions.reason: Daniel Nechita's own room on King Street since 2019 — scratch-made brunch, paninis and a house coffee blend nobody else in Knutsford is pouring.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor, HappyCow and Yell: Neki Cafe, 19 King Street, Knutsford WA16 6DW, independent family-run café owned by Daniel Nechita since 2019. Single site as of this research (a second Alderley Edge site is reported as planned/upcoming in a separate alderleyedge.com article but not yet open, so not itself included here or double-counted). Fills a real gap: Knutsford's Eat coverage is thinner than it looks on paper — King Street Kitchen (previously the only other real Eat-category brunch venue besides LI~LY) is flagged as likely closed in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json (Tripadvisor/HappyCow both mark it CLOSED), so this is a genuine like-for-like replacement gap, not padding. High confidence — long-running, multiple independent listings agree it's currently open.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Mobberley Village Bakers
suggestions.reason: Thirty-four years trading under the Goostrey's name on Town Lane, and still the reason half the village has flour on its hands before nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House-linked directory listings (Goostrey Bakery Limited, 12 employees), Yell, Restaurantji and Facebook: Mobberley Village Bakers (trading as Goostrey's), 103 Town Lane, Mobberley, Knutsford WA16 7EU — single site, ~34 years trading, no other shop locations found despite the 'Goostrey's' name (a personal/family name, not a second town). Coordinates are the real WA16 7EU postcode centroid, which sits within Mobberley's own territory (close to the existing Waugh Brow Farm Shop/Barnshaw Smithy entries), not Knutsford, despite the postal town on the address. High confidence — long-established, multiple independent directory listings agree it's currently trading.

suggestions.name: Ancoats Coffee Co
suggestions.reason: Roasting on site inside Royal Mills since 2013 — the beans leave for cafés across the city every morning, but the counter seats here still get the first pour.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the roastery's own site (ancoats-coffee.co.uk), Yelp (2026 reviews), Tripadvisor and European Coffee Trip: Ancoats Coffee Co, Unit 9/12 Royal Mills, 17 Redhill Street, Ancoats, Manchester M4 5BA — independent specialty roastery and coffee shop since 2013, single retail site (wholesale supply to other cafés doesn't count as a second location). Fills a real gap: Ancoats was the last Manchester district sitting just under the 10-venue standing-priority threshold (9). High confidence — long-established, well-reviewed, no closure signals.
